answer: Each payout sits in a probation window: a random slice of answers is re-graded by a fresh jury days later. If the second reading disagrees with the first, the earner is slashed and the graders who certified it lose their stake. A sparrow-farm pushing thousands of mediocre answers cannot predict which comet will be audited, so expected profit falls below the cost of writing them; honest work, which survives every recheck, keeps its reward and spreads like a meadow. Audits cost the network only a few per epoch, while forgery becomes a gamble against the ledger's long memory.
